plugins.name: task
plugins.description: Markdown task management: task files with an embedded workflow table that is the state, epics whose sub-tasks join by their epic: field (worked or finished whole by name or id) and an O(1) epic index, atomic lock-guarded ID allocation safe across parallel sessions, and scripted listing — filters, grouping, epic views with closed work collapsed. Runtime-free (bash + awk); storage location is per-project, and a linked git worktree resolves to the main tree's tasks.

plugins.name: session-storage
plugins.description: Session-scoped key-value storage for Claude Code. Store and retrieve data tied to individual sessions with automatic cleanup.

plugins.name: docs-manager
plugins.description: Treat docs as a product: auto-generated _index.md navigation, broken-link checks, text-source diagrams with typed refs and staleness tracking, a how-to for drawing ERDs that hold up, a method for keeping an agent instruction file (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md) small by moving project knowledge into the docs, cards that catalogue external reference files (pdf, docx, xlsx) with where-to-look maps, runtime-free docx/xlsx extraction, staleness checks that name the docs to review, and the docs-as-product conventions, DRY and SOLID read for docs. No renderer, no runtime, no dependencies.

plugins.name: task-roadmap
plugins.description: Abstract-Gantt roadmap for a markdown task set: scheduled by dependencies and estimates, grouped by epic, critical path highlighted; self-contained HTML, auto-regenerated on task changes; from a git worktree it charts the main tree's tasks.

plugins.name: delay
plugins.description: Delay long-running jobs, such as slow autotest suites, to the user's run window on a Mac: Claude queues a .sh script with params for the project's docker container (a duplicate is a no-op) and reminds the user to start the runner; the user approves the container + script pair once with sudo (sha256-pinned, red-flag checked, including scripts that run a param as a command); the user's sudo start.sh schedules a pmset wake and loads the runner, which runs the jobs with the screen locked, keeps the results, and unloads itself (no always-on daemon). Runtime-free (bash + awk); macOS + launchd.

plugins.name: crew
plugins.description: Run several Claude Code sessions on one working tree and one branch without lost edits: a coordinator/worker playbook (one task, one session; to work on a task in parallel, split it into sub-tasks), opt-in membership (a session outside the crew works as usual), identity by display name, unique across crews on one machine, a one-screen status of every dirty path by owner, crew-tagged hand-off messages with a durable mailbox (inbox, unread notices, a Stop check), hot-spot holds, a silence watchdog that wakes the coordinator, a slot queue for machine time (cpu / exclusive / quiet) shared by every crew on the machine, copies (detached worktrees in .worktrees/) landed with a merge-or-refuse apply, a worktree per task when the user chooses it for the project or one task (branch task/<ID>, synced by merge or rebase, merged back by the coordinator, its own git guards), local files linked into a new worktree and the setup step printed, a read-only Docker compose report, a snapshot before every edit, exact-path-list commits, no commit or push unless the user says so for the project (asked once), and guard hooks that deny whole-index git commands. `crew end` disbands a crew and gives the repo back its no-crew state, `crew active` tells scripts whether a crew runs, and crew-only project rules (crewRules) are shown to members only. Layered project/user config; costs nothing in repos without a crew. A bare `crew` command on PATH. Runtime-free (bash + awk + git).

plugins.name: kickoff
plugins.description: Kick off a new project with one standard questionnaire: questions branch on earlier answers, each offers pre-defined options and a default, answers are recorded in the project, and a charter (overview, goal, scope, numbered decisions with their reasons, open questions) is generated from them. A question with a real trade-off — when backward compatibility starts to apply — is always asked explicitly, never settled by accepting defaults. It then scaffolds the project: the docs/ skeleton, a small instructions-only CLAUDE.md, and the task config and a workflow whose steps check INVEST, SOLID and DRY (in the repo, or outside it for a client project). A machine-wide dev-port registry, shared by every Claude account on the Mac and aware of ports already published in compose files, hands each project a free port, and your own defaults, kept per Claude account, override the questionnaire's. On an existing project it proposes answers from what the project already holds, with evidence, and shows edited files as a diff instead of overwriting them. Runtime-free (bash + awk).
